architecture/audio-capture.html.title: Audio capture | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/audio-capture.html.summary:
Audio capture CaptureCoordinator starts and stops three recorders, picks the main track when recording ends and writes the recovery file. Each recorder implements an interface (IProcessCapture, IDeviceCapture, IMicCapture), and the tests use doubles instead. The three recorders Recorder API WAV format Temporary file ProcessLoopbackRecorder WASAPI process loopback (own COM interop in Interop/) 16-bit PCM, 44.1 kHz, stereo (AUTOCONVERTPCM) recording_.wav DeviceLoopbackRecorder NAudio WasapiLoopbackCapture on the default output, Console and Communications roles (not duplicated when they are the same device) The device's native format recording__console.wav, recording__communications.wav MicrophoneRecorder NAudio WasapiCapture on the default input (Multimedia role) The device's native format recording__mic.wav They all write to %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber\, with = yyyyMMdd_HHmmss. Process loopback Wasapi.ActivateProcessLoopbackAsync(pid, includeProcessTree) activates a virtual IAudioClient with AUDIOCLIENT_ACTIVATION_TYPE_PROCESS_LOOPBACK and the INCLUDE_TARGET_PROCESS_TREE mode. This API exists from Windows 10 build 20348 onwards. The client is initialized in shared mode with LOOPBACK | EVENTCALLBACK | AUTOCONVERTPCM | SRC_DEFAULT_QUALITY. A dedicated thread (LoopbackTranscriber-Capture) waits for the sample event and writes each packet to the WAV. Besides being written to disk, each block is published on the AudioCaptured event, which feeds live translation. Only this recorder publishes it: the live session only hears the application. The WAV is opened with FileShare.ReadWrite | FileShare.Delete and a placeholder header. The real sizes are written when recording stops. If the application dies before then, the header stays at zero and orphan recovery repairs it. When stopping, it waits 5 s for the thread. If it does not finish, it stops the IAudioClient and waits another 5 s. If it still does not finish, it abandons the session: it fixes the header with what was written so far and returns the file. A hung driver never blocks the application. If the capture ended with an error but there is data, the audio is kept and a warning is logged. With no data, ErrorAudioCapture is thrown. Which process is recorded TargetProcessWatcher checks the watched applications (TargetApp.ProcessNames) every 1.5 s. For each one: Process.GetProcessesByName with each candidate name, for example ms-teams and then Teams. ProcessTree.FindRootProcessId keeps the root process among those found. AudioSessionFinder.FindActiveProcessId looks among the active audio sessions for one belonging to those processes. If there is one, that PID is used. The Applications screen uses AudioSessionFinder.ListRunningApps() to list processes that have an audio session. Time gaps: CaptureTimeline WASAPI delivers no packets when nothing is playing. Written as-is, the WAV would get shorter and the tracks would drift apart. CaptureTimeline compares each packet's timestamp (QPC) with the samples already written: If more than 250 ms are missing, it fills the gap with silence (WriteSilence) before the packet. It keeps FirstSampleTimestamp, the instant of the first sample, which is used to align the microphone. Packets flagged AUDCLNT_BUFFERFLAGS_TIMESTAMP_ERROR are not used to measure gaps. NAudio devices, which provide no timestamp, use the arrival time minus the packet duration. Start (StartAsync) Generates baseName = recording_ and marks it as owned, so orphan recovery does not touch it while recording. Starts the process capture. If that fails, recording does not start and the error reaches the user. Writes recording_.session.json with the application and the time. If it cannot, it warns with WarningRecoveryFileNotWritten. Starts the device capture. If that fails, it is logged and recording continues without it. Starts the microphone. If that fails, it warns with WarningMicNotRecorded. Rewrites the .session.json with the start time of each track. Stop (StopAsync) Stops the three captures: the process first, then the device and the microphone, each on the thread pool. A failure in one does not prevent stopping the others. The microphone waits at most 3 s for RecordingStopped, and so does each device channel. Then: Choosing the main track flowchart LR A([On stop]) --> B{"Does the process track
have a peak ≥ 0.01?"} B -->|yes| P[Process track] B -->|no| C{"Does any output track
have a peak ≥ 0.01?"} C -->|yes| D["Output track with
the highest peak"] C -->|no| E["Process track,
even if silent"] class P,D ok class E fail The threshold is CaptureCoordinator.DeviceSignalThreshold = 0.01, on a 0-to-1 scale. If the microphone track does not exceed that same threshold, MicrophoneRecorder deletes it when stopping. Microphone offset The microphone track starts at a different instant from the main one. The offset (MicStartOffset) is computed: from the first-sample timestamps of each track (FirstSampleTimestamp), if both exist; otherwise, from the difference between the start times of each capture. The result is a StoppedRecording: main track, microphone, offset, all paths, the stop error if any, the baseName and the warnings. After processing On success, DeleteOriginals deletes all the temporary WAVs and the .session.json, and releases the baseName. On failure, PreserveFailed moves the main track and the microphone to FailedRecordingStore. If even that is not possible, the originals stay in the temporary folder and recovery will find them on the next start. Every time DeleteOriginals runs, it also calls DeleteStaleRecordings, which deletes the recording_*.16k.wav files (derived files for Whisper) older than 7 days left in the temporary folder.

architecture/live-translation.html.title: Live translation | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/live-translation.html.summary:
Live translation The live session (LiveTranscriptionSession) turns the application audio, while recording, into transcribed and translated lines. It is independent from the final transcription: it does not change the recording or its result. Pipeline flowchart TB A["ProcessLoopbackRecorder.AudioCaptured
PCM 44.1 kHz stereo"] --> Q[("Audio channel
3000 blocks")] Q --> S["LiveAudioSegmenter
16 kHz mono · VAD"] S -->|"chunks and drafts"| T[LiveTranscriberStage] T -->|"lines and drafts"| R[LiveTranslatorStage] T <-->|"stdin/stdout @@L"| W1[["Worker process
whisper-live"]] R <-->|"stdin/stdout @@L"| W2[["Worker process
translate-live"]] T --> UI["LiveSessionController
→ LiveTranscriptModel"] R --> UI class W1,W2 io class UI ok LiveSessionController.Start creates the session with: Whisper: the same model as the final transcription, the meeting language (ResolveMeetingLanguage), GPU, and LiveAudioContext and LiveFlashAttention from the settings. Translator: the summary model, if present, with cores / 2 threads between 2 and 6. If it is not present, the session only transcribes. Session events arrive from background threads. The controller marshals them to the UI thread and drops those from a session that is no longer the current one. 1. Segmentation (LiveAudioSegmenter) It receives 16-bit PCM at 44.1 kHz stereo, mixes it down to mono and resamples to 16 kHz by averaging. It works in 20 ms frames (320 samples): a frame is speech if its level is above −42 dBFS. Rule Value Pre-roll when speech is detected 10 frames (200 ms) End of chunk on a pause 30 frames (600 ms) of silence, or 15 frames (300 ms) if the chunk already lasts 3 s Minimum speech to emit a chunk 20 frames (400 ms) Trailing silence kept up to 10 frames (200 ms) Maximum length 500 frames (10 s). It is cut at the quietest frame within the last 3 s. Draft when the chunk has at least 25 speech frames and either 40 frames (800 ms) have passed since the last draft without reaching 10 silent frames in a row, or it has just reached 8 silent frames with more than 3 new speech frames since the last draft A draft is the chunk in progress, still open, that is transcribed to show provisional text. Each draft carries a sequence number (DraftSeq). If the final chunk exactly covers the last draft (with a 3-speech-frame tolerance), it says so, so that its text can be reused. 2. Transcription (LiveTranscriberStage) It uses a LiveWorkMailbox: a bounded queue of 8 final chunks that drops the oldest when full, plus a single draft slot where the latest draft replaces the previous one. Priority. Final chunks go before drafts. The exception is when the pending draft is exactly the one preceding that final chunk. Generations. Each final chunk advances a counter (LiveGeneration). A draft transcribed after a newer final chunk has arrived is discarded, so old text is never shown over newer text. Reuse. If a final chunk covers the last transcribed draft, its text is used without calling Whisper again. The metrics mark it as chunk-reused. A final line identical to the previous one, ignoring case, is not repeated. LiveTextSplitter splits each final line: if it is 90 characters or longer, it is cut at sentence ends (., !, ?, …) into pieces of at least 28 characters. The whisper-live worker keeps the model loaded for the whole session. Each request carries the 16 kHz PCM in base64. The worker pads it with silence up to 1 s if shorter and applies the same segment filters as the final transcription, with a no-speech threshold of 0.6. 3. Translation (LiveTranslatorStage) It uses another queue, of 6 lines, with a draft slot. A line dropped because the queue is full is marked as not translated (TranslationSkipped) instead of waiting forever. Each line is translated with the previous line as context, which is not translated itself. Drafts are translated too, to show a provisional translation. If the final line was not split and matches the last translated draft, that translation is reused (translation-reused in the metrics). Changing the target language applies to whatever is queued from then on. The translate-live worker loads Qwen3-4B with a 2048-token context, temperature 0.2, top-k 20 and top-p 0.9, and a token limit that depends on the text length (between 64 and 400). The prompt asks it to act as an interpreter that returns only the translation. It includes /no_think and an empty, pre-filled block so Qwen3 does not reason before answering. Before announcing itself as ready, it translates a test sentence to warm the model up. 4. Worker supervision (LiveWorkerSupervisor) Situation Reaction The worker answers a request with Error It is logged and that chunk or line is skipped. A timeout (60 s for Whisper, 30 s for translation) or the process dies The worker is restarted, at most 3 times per session. The worker is not ready within 180 s The session reports the error. Further failures The window shows the error. The recording carries on unchanged. Metrics Each chunk and each translation is written to %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\live-metrics.log. Each line starts with the date and time: Line Fields chunk (or chunk-reused when it reuses the draft, draft for a draft) audio seconds of audio · whisper processing seconds · rtf processing over audio · latency delay since speech ended · queue queued chunks · dropped dropped · chars characters translation (or draft-translation) chars characters · model translation seconds · latency delay · queue queued lines translation-reused chars characters When the session closes, a SUMMARY line is added with the model, whether the GPU was used, the audio context, flash attention, the dropped and reused chunks, and the 50th and 90th latency percentiles for chunks, drafts and translations. The window shows the same data in its technical strip (LiveMetricsPresenter). Dropped audio The input channel holds at most 3000 blocks and drops the oldest. This only happens if the segmenter stalls, which should not happen because it only does in-memory computation. The first drop is logged once in app.log.

architecture/localization.html.title: Localization | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/localization.html.summary: Localization The interface is available in Spanish, English, Portuguese, German and Russian. All texts live in a single class, Services/Strings.cs. A build-time check guarantees that no key is missing and none is left over. Strings Each key holds one text per language. For example, RecordStart is "Iniciar grabación" in Spanish and "Start recording" in English, and it also has its Portuguese, German and Russian versions. Member Used for Strings.Instance Single instance. Implements INotifyPropertyChanged. Get(key) / Format(key, args) Text in the current language. GetIn(lang, key) / FormatIn(lang, key, args) Text in a given language. Used by log messages (in English) and by the summary labels. this[key] For XAML: {Binding Path=[RecordStart], Source={x:Static services:Strings.Instance}}. SetLanguage(lang) Changes the language, raises Item[] (WPF refreshes every binding) and fires LanguageChanged. If a language lacks a key, English is used. If the key does not exist, the key itself is returned. The build check stops either case from reaching a published version. Changing the language in Settings takes effect immediately. MainViewModel forwards LanguageChanged to the viewer and the recording so they rebuild the texts that do not come from a binding, such as the status and the speaker labels. What is not translated when saving So that files do not depend on the language of whoever recorded them: Speaker labels in the .md: always Participantes, Tu and <name> (Tú) (SpeakerLabels). The viewer translates them when displaying them. Default application name: Meeting is stored and shown through DefaultAppName ("Meeting", "Reunión"…). The old reunion is accepted too. Errors: stored with their key, not their text. See Reliability. The summary, on the other hand, is written in the interface language at the time it is generated, with the section labels already translated. When displaying it, the viewer replaces the section titles with those of the current language (SummaryFormatter). Build-time check (Build/LocalizationCheck.targets) An inline MSBuild task (RoslynCodeTaskFactory) runs before CoreCompile. It reads Strings.cs, every .cs in the project and every XAML file (Page and ApplicationDefinition). Code Level What it detects LT0000 error No key was found: the format of Strings.cs has changed and the task cannot read it. LT0001 error A key is used that does not exist. LT0002 error A key is missing a language, or has it empty. LT0003 warning A key is not used anywhere. LT0004 error Duplicate key. These count as uses of a key: Strings.Instance.Get("X"), Format("X", …), GetIn(lang, "X"), FormatIn(lang, "X", …) and Strings.Instance["X"]; UserMessage.FromKey("X", …) and UserError.<method>("X", …) or UserError.<method>(inner, "X", …); in XAML, Binding [X] … Source={x:Static …:Strings.Instance}; any literal starting with a prefix from KeyLiteralPrefixes: currently SummaryLabel, because those keys are built in a switch. So that a key passed through a variable is not flagged as unused, any C# literal identical to a key counts as a use. The task is skipped in the temporary _wpftmp project that WPF generates when compiling XAML. It can also be turned off with -p:SkipLocalizationCheck=true. Adding a language Add the ["xx"] = "…" translation to every key in Strings.cs. The check reports each one that is missing. Add xx to Languages="es;en;pt;de;ru" in LocalizationCheck.targets. Add it to AvailableUiLanguages (ConfigViewModel), to AppSettings.DetectSystemLanguage, to LiveTranslationPreferences.SupportedLanguages, to the language list and LanguageNameFor (English name for the translator) in LiveTranslationViewModel, and to the language list and sample texts (PreviewSamples) in LiveTranslationSettingsViewModel. Add its name to SummarizationService.GetSummaryLanguageName, which gives the language name for the prompt. Add the language to the installer's [Languages] if Inno Setup has a translation for it.

architecture/models.html.summary: Models and integrity The two models Transcription Summary and translation Model Whisper large-v3-turbo, GGML q5_1 Qwen3-4B, GGUF Q4_K_M Source huggingface.co/sandrohanea/whisper.net, q5_1 folder huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-4B-GGUF Pinned revision 79dea24237e62d8a6e20a978ba415446d19712b3 bc640142c66e1fdd12af0bd68f40445458f3869b SHA256 05265418cae607e28c62db4095612e2c1967885d87cbda5a104834414b563ac8 7485fe6f11af29433bc51cab58009521f205840f5b4ae3a32fa7f92e8534fdf5 Pinned in WhisperTranscriptionService.ModelRevision and PinnedSha256 SummarizationService.ModelRevision and ModelSha256 Local file <ModelsFolder>\whisper\ggml-turbo.bin <ModelsFolder>\llm\Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf The URLs point to a specific commit (…/resolve/<revision>/…), not to main. If the source repository is updated, the application keeps downloading exactly the same file. Download EnsureModelDownloadedAsync works the same way in both services: If the file already exists and passes verification (see below), it is done. Downloads to <destination>.download in 1 MB blocks. If a .download from an earlier attempt already exists, it resumes with a Range header; if the server does not answer 206, it starts from scratch. The .download is only kept when the download is cancelled (which is what Pause does) or the application closes halfway. A network or disk error deletes it. Reports progress at most every 200 ms. If the bytes received do not match Content-Length, throws ErrorDownloadIncomplete. Computes the SHA256 of the .download. If it does not match, deletes it and throws ErrorModelHashMismatch. Moves the .download to the destination and writes the verification marker. For Whisper, if the download fails it is retried once before throwing ErrorModelDownloadFailed. A model without a pinned hash is never downloaded: ErrorModelNotPinned is thrown. Verifying without recomputing the hash every time Computing the SHA256 of 2.5 GB takes a while. ModelIntegrity stores a <model>.verified.json marker next to each model: Field What it stores Sha256 The hash the file was checked against. Length The file size in bytes when it was checked. LastWriteTimeUtcTicks The file's modification date (UTC, in ticks) when it was checked. EnsureVerifiedAsync(path, expectedHash): If the marker matches the expected hash and the file's current size and modification time, the model is accepted without reading it. Otherwise it recomputes the SHA256: if it matches, it writes the marker and accepts the model; if it does not match, it deletes the model and its marker and returns false so it gets downloaded again. Verifications of the same file are serialized with one semaphore per path. If a model exists but cannot be loaded (WhisperModelLoadException or LoadWeightsFailedException), ModelIntegrity.LoadFailed deletes the marker and throws ErrorModelLoadFailed. On the next use the hash is recomputed: if the file is damaged it is deleted and downloaded again; if not, the problem lies elsewhere (GPU, memory). Verification at startup MainViewModel.Start runs IModelVerifier.VerifyInstalledModelsAsync in the background: It checks both installed models with EnsureVerifiedAsync. Usually reading the marker is enough. If one was damaged and deleted, it goes back to the first-run screen. It does not do so while a recording is in progress or being processed. If a model cannot be read (locked, no permissions), it warns with NoticeModelVerificationFailed and leaves it alone: it will be checked again before use. Updating a model On the file's Hugging Face page, copy the file's commit and SHA256. Change the revision and the hash together: Whisper: ModelRevision and the GgmlType.LargeV3Turbo entry of PinnedSha256 in WhisperTranscriptionService.Download.cs. Qwen3: ModelRevision and ModelSha256 in SummarizationService.Download.cs. If the file name changes, also ModelDownloadUrl, ModelName and AppSettings.SummaryModelFileName. Update the sizes in the FirstRun*ModelSize and Config*ModelName texts in Strings.cs. Users who already have the previous model will find that their marker does not match the new hash. The model will be rehashed, deleted, and the new one downloaded. To support another Whisper size (small, medium…), it is enough to add its hash to PinnedSha256. ParseModelSize already recognizes the names.

Presentation only: window, tray, calendar, floating window. ViewModels/ State and commands of each screen. They do not know the views. Services/ Logic: capture, processing, transcription, summary, live session, persistence, localization and logging. Models/ Plain data: settings, watched applications, history items, speaker labels. Interop/ WASAPI COM interfaces, process loopback activation, audio sessions and the process tree. Build/ LocalizationCheck.targets: build-time translation check. Root Program, App, AppServices (container), CrashHandler, SingleInstance. Design principles Nothing leaves the computer. The only network access is downloading the two models, from fixed Hugging Face revisions and with their SHA256 checked. See Models and integrity. No audio is lost. A recording that cannot be transcribed is kept to be retried, also when the application closes, hangs or the computer shuts down. See Reliability. Inference runs in separate processes. Whisper and LLamaSharp allocate native and GPU memory that is not always released when the model is unloaded. Each transcription and each summary runs in a child process that exits when done. That keeps the main application light while it waits in the tray. See Worker processes. Services do not depend on WPF. RecordingWorkflow, RecordingProcessor, CaptureCoordinator and the parts of the live session (segmenter, work queue, line splitting) are tested without a window. Dependencies on the system (capture, Whisper, audio conversion, dialogs, dispatcher, process watcher) sit behind interfaces that the tests replace with test doubles. Child ViewModels do not know each other. The shell (MainViewModel) coordinates them, and they talk to each other through messages. See ViewModels and messaging. Main dependencies Package Version Used for CommunityToolkit.Mvvm 8.4.2 ObservableObject, [ObservableProperty], [RelayCommand], WeakReferenceMessenger. Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection 10.0.0 Service container. WPF-UI 4.3.0 Dark theme, accent color and Fluent controls. In addition: MemoryTrimmer.Release() compacts the heap and trims the working set: after each transcription and each summary, when a recording finishes processing, when the window is minimized or hidden, and once 4 s after it is first shown. BackgroundMemoryTrimmer trims the working set every 5 minutes while the window is minimized or hidden in the tray.

architecture/processing.html.summary:
Processing a recording The flow: RecordingWorkflow RecordingWorkflow does not depend on WPF. It chains capture, processing and saving, and decides what to do with the audio if something fails. temp files"] G -->|no| I["Leaves the originals
in %TEMP%"] class F ok class E,P fail class H,I io Method Used for StartAsync(pid, appName) Starts the capture. Returns the start-up warnings, such as the microphone not being recorded. StopAndProcessAsync(appName, recordedAt, callbacks) Normal stop: processes, saves and cleans up. On failure, keeps the audio. StopAndPreserveAsync(appName, recordedAt, reason) Stops and keeps the audio unprocessed. Used on exit, on shutdown and on errors. RetryAsync(failedRecording, callbacks) Processes a preserved recording. On success, removes it from the store. ListFailed() / DiscardFailed(recording) Unprocessed recordings. RecoverOrphans() Recovery at startup. See Reliability. The summary is not part of this flow: it is generated manually from the viewer. Processing: RecordingProcessor ProcessAsync(sourceWav, micWav, micStartOffset, settings, callbacks) takes the tracks and returns the final text. It uses IWhisperTranscriber and IAudioPreparer, which the tests replace. Model. EnsureModelDownloadedAsync checks the model and downloads it if missing. Status: "Checking the transcription model...". Conversion. Both tracks are converted to 16-bit PCM WAV, 16 kHz, mono (AudioConverter.ConvertToWhisperFormat: 50% mono mixdown and WDL resampling) into .16k.wav. Noise gate on the microphone. ApplyNoiseGate silences the 50 ms windows whose RMS level is more than 34 dB below the track's peak, with 10 ms fades at each change. If it fails, the track is transcribed unfiltered. Transcription of both tracks (see below). Combined progress is the average of the two. Microphone activity. Microphone segments with less than 15% active windows, or less than 0.15 s active, are dropped (GetActivityMap, 50 ms windows). Echo filter between the microphone and the application (see below). Composition of the text with speaker labels. If the text is empty and the audio is 20 s or longer, ErrorNoTextInAudio is thrown: the recording is kept as failed. If it is shorter, the empty text is returned: TranscriptSaver saves nothing and RecordingWorkflow deletes the temporary files as for any finished recording. The .16k.wav files are always deleted at the end, in a finally. Language MeetingLanguage Application track Microphone Execution "" (default) application language same In parallel, each with half the threads. es, en, pt, de, ru that one that one In parallel. auto detected the one detected on the application track In sequence: first the application, then the microphone with that language. Detection (LanguageDetector) measures the level of each second of the track and tries 30 s windows starting every 5 s. It keeps the 3 with the most active seconds, at least 8 and without overlapping. On each it calls Whisper's DetectLanguageWithProbability and adds up the probability of the language returned. The confidence is the winning language's total divided by the number of windows. If it does not reach 0.5, the application language is used. The result is written to app.log. Whisper (WhisperTranscriptionService) A silent track (peak ≤ −50 dBFS) returns 0 segments without starting any process. Each transcription runs in a whisper worker process. See Worker processes. Threads per instance: cores / 2 / concurrent transcriptions, between 2 and 16. Parameters: no context between segments (WithNoContext), no-speech threshold 0.6 (0.45 for the microphone, strict mode) and probabilities enabled. Vulkan GPU when available. Per-segment filters (FilterSegmentText), in order: Drops non-speech tags such as [MUSIC] or (applause) and text with no letters or digits. Drops segments with a no-speech probability ≥ 0.6 (≥ 0.45 in strict mode). Drops typical hallucination phrases ("thank you", "gracias por ver el video", "subtitles by the amara.org community"…) if their no-speech probability is ≥ 0.3 (≥ 0.2 in strict mode). Drops text written in a different alphabet from the language's: 30% or more of the letters outside it. Only applies to Latin- and Cyrillic-script languages. It does not apply when the language is undetermined. Removes phrases repeated in a loop (RemovePhraseLoops) and drops repetitions of a single word (IsRepeatedWordLoop). On the whole set: RemoveRepeatedSegments removes repeated segments and MergeCloseSegments joins those separated by 2 s or less, up to 400 characters. Echo filter (MeetingEchoFilter) With speakers, the microphone also picks up the participants, and with headphones the application sometimes plays back your own voice. For each microphone segment of 3 words or more: Finds the overlapping application segments, with a ±3 s margin, once the microphone offset is applied. If they share at least 60% of their words, they are the same sentence. If not, the segment is left as it is. Decides who spoke first. The microphone is the original if it starts 300 ms or more earlier, or if it starts within 150 ms and is loud. Loud means its 75th-percentile level is within 10 dB of the 90th percentile of the whole track (MicLoudness). If the microphone is the original, it is kept, and the application segments that are 60% or more contained in it are removed. Otherwise, the microphone segment is dropped as echo. Composition (TranscriptComposer) Sorts all segments by start time. Microphone segments are shifted by MicStartOffset. Starts a new paragraph when the speaker changes, after a pause of 3 s or more, or when the paragraph exceeds 700 characters. If there is any microphone segment, each paragraph starts with a label: Participantes:, Tu: or (Tú):. Otherwise the text has no labels. Labels are always stored in Spanish (SpeakerLabels) so the file does not depend on the interface language. The viewer translates them when displaying them (SpeakerDisplay). Saving: TranscriptSaver It writes to \\_\: File Contents .md The header # - dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm, a blank line and the text. .wav Copy of the main track. _mic.wav Copy of the microphone, if there is one. .recording.json MicStartOffsetTicks, only if there is a microphone. is the application name with characters that are invalid in a file name replaced by _ (TranscriptHistoryService.GetAppFolderName). If the text is empty, nothing is saved. Re-transcription (TranscriptRetranscriber) Takes .wav, _mic.wav if it exists, and the offset from .recording.json, or 0 if there is none. Runs RecordingProcessor.ProcessAsync with the current settings, in a work folder %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber\retranscribe\ that is deleted at the end. Rewrites the .md, keeping its header. Old transcripts in .txt are rewritten as .txt. Unlike a new recording, an empty result is always an error, whatever the duration.

architecture/reliability.html.title: Reliability | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/reliability.html.summary: Reliability The goal is that no recording is ever lost: if it cannot be transcribed now, its audio is kept so it can be retried later. This page lists every path by which a recording can be left half-done and what happens in each one. Unprocessed recordings (FailedRecordingStore) A preserved recording is a folder under %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\failed\: The folder name is the recording date plus 8 random characters, for example 20261018_093000_1a2b3c4d. Inside: File Contents manifest.json AppName, RecordedAt, SourceWav, MicWav, MicStartOffsetTicks, Error, ErrorKey and ErrorArgs. meeting.wav The main track. microphone.wav The microphone, if there was one. TryPreserve creates the folder, writes the manifest and moves the WAVs. If it cannot move the microphone, it keeps only the main track and warns. If the main track fails, it undoes what it did and returns null, and the originals stay where they were. List reads the manifests and skips folders without meeting.wav. An unreadable manifest raises a notice (NoticeUnreadableFailedRecording) and the folder is left untouched. The error is stored with its localization key (ErrorKey, ErrorArgs), so the reason is shown in the current language even if it has changed since. Retry (RecordingWorkflow.RetryAsync) processes the recording with the current settings and, on success, deletes the folder. If it fails again, the folder stays as it was. Discard deletes it after asking for confirmation. RecordingViewModel shows, in each application's view, the recordings with that AppName and, in every view, those with the default name (Meeting). Every path, covered What happens Where it is handled Outcome Transcription fails (model, GPU, no text in ≥ 20 s) RecordingWorkflow.StopAndProcessAsync The audio becomes unprocessed, with the reason. No text in a recording of < 20 s RecordingProcessor.ProcessAsync The only exception: not a failure. Nothing is saved and the audio is deleted. The user exits while recording and chooses No AppExitWorkflow → PreserveInterruptedRecordingAsync (10 s) Unprocessed (RecordingInterruptedReason). Windows signs out or shuts down MainWindow.OnSessionEnding → PreserveInterruptedRecording (3 s) Unprocessed. Unhandled exception on the UI thread CrashHandler → PreserveInterruptedRecording (3 s) Unprocessed. The message confirms it (CrashBodyPreserved). Unhandled exception on another thread CrashHandler → rescue on the UI thread (2 s to respond) Unprocessed if there is time. The process dies abruptly (power cut, Task Manager) OrphanRecordingRecovery on the next start Unprocessed (RecordingRecoveredReason). It cannot be moved to failed\ CaptureCoordinator.PreserveFailed The originals stay in %TEMP% and the next start recovers them. The audio driver hangs when stopping ProcessLoopbackRecorder.AbandonStuckCapture The WAV is closed with what was captured and things carry on. The synchronous rescues (PreserveInterruptedRecording) are used where await is not possible, such as the error handler or SessionEnding. They run the work on the thread pool and wait with a time limit. Since they never need the calling thread, they cannot deadlock. Orphan recordings A recording is an orphan if its audio is in %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber but no instance is recording it. MainViewModel.Start calls RecordingViewModel.RecoverOrphanRecordingsAsync, which runs OrphanRecordingRecovery.Run: Finds the recording_*.session.json files (and grabacion_*, the prefix used by older versions) and the WAVs with a recording name that have no .session.json. Skips those that belong to the current instance (CaptureCoordinator._ownedBaseNames). Defers those with any WAV in use, checked by opening it with FileShare.None. It retries up to 4 times, every 30 s. If they are still in use, they are left for the next start. For each one: Reads the session. Without a .session.json, the application is Meeting and the date is taken from the file name. Ignores derived WAVs (.16k.wav) and those with no data beyond the header (WavRepair.HasAudioData). Repairs the header of each WAV (WavRepair.TryRepairHeader). If the data size is 0 or larger than the file, it writes the real size, rounded down to blockAlign, and fixes the RIFF size. Picks the track with the same rule as a normal stop: the process track if its peak is ≥ 0.01; otherwise the output track with the highest peak ≥ 0.01; otherwise the process track even if silent. Only when there is neither a process nor an output track does the microphone become the main track. See Audio capture. Computes the microphone offset from the times saved in the session. Moves the tracks to failed\ and deletes the rest. If there is no audio, deletes everything silently. Failures are reported with NoticeOrphanRecoveryFailed. Their audio stays in %TEMP% and they are retried on the next start. Settings SettingsService keeps the settings in memory as JSON: each Snapshot() is an independent copy, and each Update(change) applies the change to a new copy under a lock. Atomic write: settings.json.tmp and then File.Replace, or File.Move the first time. No pointless writes: if the JSON has not changed, nothing is written. Retries: 3 attempts, waiting 100 ms × attempt. If they all fail, the changes stay pending in memory, the user is told once (NoticeSettingsNotSaved), and it is retried on the next change and in App.OnExit (FlushPendingWrite). Damaged file: renamed to settings.json.corrupt-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>, defaults are used and the user is told (NoticeSettingsReset). Errors that mean something to the user UserError creates ordinary exceptions (InvalidOperationException, InvalidDataException, IOException) with their localization key and arguments in Exception.Data. The Message is in English, for the log. UserMessage.From(ex) recovers the key, and Localize() translates it into the current language when displayed. An exception without a key is shown as ErrorUnexpected with its message. Keys travel intact through the worker processes (ErrorKey and ErrorArgs) and through the unprocessed recordings (manifest.json). Expected failures and programming errors ExpectedFailures groups the exceptions that count as environment failures: Predicate Exceptions IsFile IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException IsAudioFile the above, plus FormatException and InvalidDataException IsDeviceOrFile COMException, InvalidComObjectException, IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException The code's catch blocks filter with these predicates (catch (Exception ex) when (ExpectedFailures.IsFile(ex))). A programming error, such as a NullReferenceException, is not hidden: it reaches CrashHandler and ends up in the log.

architecture/startup.html.title: Startup and shutdown | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/startup.html.summary:
Startup and shutdown Entry point Program.Main ([STAThread]) first decides whether the process is the application or a worker process: flowchart LR A(["Program.Main"]) --> B{"Is args[1] --worker
with 5 or more arguments?"} B -->|yes| W["WorkerHost.Run
and Environment.Exit with its code"] B -->|no| C["new App()
InitializeComponent · Run"] class W io class C ok A worker process never creates App or any window. App.xaml is declared as a Page and not as an ApplicationDefinition (the .csproj does this) so that this is the Main used, not the one WPF generates. That way a worker process starts without loading anything from the UI. See Worker processes. App.OnStartup In this order: CrashHandler.Install subscribes to DispatcherUnhandledException, AppDomain.UnhandledException and TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException. It comes first so it also covers startup itself. SingleInstance.TryAcquire takes the Local\LoopbackTranscriber-B6E1F6C4-… mutex. If another instance already holds it, it signals that instance's …-Activate event (with AllowSetForegroundWindow so it can come to the front) and this one exits. A mutex abandoned by an instance that crashed is taken over anyway. Settings: creates UserNotices and SettingsService. EnsureDefaultUserName() suggests the Windows name the first time, and the language is set with Strings.Instance.SetLanguage(...). Theme: WPF-UI dark, with the #6A2BD9 accent. Container: AppServices.Build(settings, notices) registers every service and ViewModel and validates the graph when building it (ValidateOnBuild = true). Resolves MainWindow, registers it with CrashHandler.Attach together with RecordingViewModel so the recording can be rescued, starts listening for activations from other instances and shows the window. The MainWindow constructor calls MainViewModel.Start(), which: starts the process watcher (TargetsViewModel.Start); loads the history; starts, in the background, the recovery of orphan recordings and the verification of the installed models. The container (AppServices) Everything is a singleton except the ViewModels of the secondary pages, which are transient and created on demand through IPageFactory: Registration Implementation ISettingsStore SettingsService (created before the container) UserNotices shared instance of user notices ITargetWatcher TargetProcessWatcher ICustomAppsService CustomAppsService ISummarizer SummarizationService IModelVerifier ModelVerifier IWhisperTranscriber WhisperTranscriptionService, which is also registered as its own type IAudioPreparer NaudioAudioPreparer TranscriptHistoryService, TranscriptsFolderWatcher — RecordingProcessor, TranscriptSaver, TranscriptRetranscriber — FailedRecordingStore folder %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\failed CaptureCoordinator with ProcessLoopbackRecorder, DeviceLoopbackRecorder, MicrophoneRecorder and the FailedRecordingStore RecordingWorkflow — IDialogService WpfDialogService IUiDispatcher WpfUiDispatcher.Instance IMessenger WeakReferenceMessenger.Default Shell ViewModels HistoryViewModel, ViewerViewModel, TargetsViewModel, RecordingViewModel, MainViewModel IRecordingHost RecordingHost ILiveTranslationFactory LiveTranslationFactory Others TrayMenuViewModel, AppExitWorkflow, UserNoticePresenter, MainWindow Transient FirstRunViewModel, ConfigViewModel, ApplicationsViewModel, LiveTranslationSettingsViewModel IPageFactory ServiceProviderPageFactory, which resolves them from the container First run or application The MainViewModel constructor checks whether both models exist, models\whisper\ggml-turbo.bin and models\llm\Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf: If they do, it sets FirstRunSetupCompleted, selects the first application and shows AppView. If not, it creates FirstRunViewModel and shows FirstRun. When that completes, it opens Config. If the startup verification deletes a damaged model, the app goes back to FirstRun, unless a recording is in progress or being processed. Shutdown There are four ways for the application to end. None of them deletes unprocessed audio. Situation What happens Window X Closing is cancelled and the window is hidden to the tray (HideToTray). Exit from the tray AppExitWorkflow.ConfirmExitAsync decides (see below). If a summary is being generated, you are asked to confirm because it would be lost. Windows sign-out or shutdown SessionEnding lets the app close and calls RecordingViewModel.PreserveInterruptedRecording(3 s): it stops the capture and keeps the audio unprocessed. Unhandled error CrashHandler preserves the recording (3 s), shows the message with the log path and exits with code 1. AppExitWorkflow Waits, for 10 s at most, for a half-started recording to finish starting. With a recording in progress, asks Yes / No / Cancel: Yes: shows the window, stops and processes (IRecordingHost.StopRecordingAsync) and exits. No: keeps the audio unprocessed (PreserveInterruptedRecordingAsync, 10 s at most) and exits. Cancel: does not exit. With a recording being processed, asks whether to wait. If accepted, it shows the window and waits until IsBusy becomes false. While an exit is pending, further exit requests are ignored. App.OnExit Disposes the container, which disposes recorders, watchers and timers. Then it writes any settings that could not be saved (FlushPendingWrite) and releases the single-instance mutex. CrashHandler Event Handling DispatcherUnhandledException (UI thread) Marks it handled, logs it, rescues the recording, shows CrashBody, CrashBodyPreserved or CrashBodyLost and closes the application. AppDomain.UnhandledException (other thread) Logs it, rescues the recording on the UI thread (giving it 2 s to respond) and shows the same message. The process ends anyway. UnobservedTaskException Only logs it and marks it observed. A second error while the first one is being handled is only logged.

architecture/summary.html.title: Summary | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/summary.html.summary:
Summary SummarizationService implements ISummarizer. ViewerViewModel calls it with the transcript text, the model path and the interface language. The result (RecordingSummary: Title and Summary) is saved to .summary.json. Where it runs SummarizeAsync serializes a SummaryJob (TranscriptText, ModelPath, UiLanguage) and runs it in a summary worker process. Progress arrives as @@P . Inside the worker, SummarizeInProcessAsync does the actual work. When the process ends, all the model's memory is released. See Worker processes. Model and parameters Parameter Value Model Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf (see Models and integrity) Context 8192 tokens GPU layers all (GpuLayerCount = 999), with the Vulkan backend if available; otherwise CPU Threads cores / 2, between 2 and 6 Executor LLamaSharp StatelessExecutor: each prompt is independent Normal sampling temperature 0.6, top-k 30, top-p 0.9, repeat penalty 1.12, frequency 0.3, presence 0.3, penalty window 512 Strong sampling temperature 0.8, repeat penalty 1.25, frequency 0.6, presence 0.5 Stop <\|im_end\|> or Steps flowchart TD T(["Transcript"]) --> L{"≤ 9000
characters?"} L -->|yes| F["Final prompt"] L -->|no| C["Split into parts
of ≤ 9000"] C --> K["Key points per part
marking OBJETIVO / PROXIMO_PASO"] K --> J["Join, ≤ 9000 characters"] J --> F F --> P["Parse TITULO / RESUMEN"] P --> R["Remove repeated lines"] R --> M{"Goals or Next steps
missing?"} M -->|yes| X["Follow-up prompts"] M -->|no| O["Translate labels"] X --> O class O ok 1. Condense if long If the transcript exceeds 9000 characters, SplitIntoChunks splits it into pieces of at most 9000. Each piece gets the Chunk prompt (at most 600 tokens), which asks for a list of key points: Goals and commitments are marked [OBJETIVO], and upcoming meetings or follow-ups [PROXIMO_PASO]. Each part is trimmed to its character quota (FitPointsToLimit). Marked points are always kept, even when the others do not fit. The parts are joined under Puntos clave (parte i de N):. The whole is trimmed to 9000 characters. 2. Final prompt The Final prompt (at most 1800 tokens) asks for plain text in exactly this format: Label Contents TITULO: The title, on the same line. RESUMEN: Marks the start of the sections. Proposito: Two or three sentences. Puntos clave: One line per point, starting with - . Temas: Each topic on a * Topic line and, below it, its details with - . Objetivos: One line per goal, with - . Proximos pasos: One line per step, with - . The prompt's rules: write in the requested language even if the transcript is in another one, between 5 and 12 key points, invent nothing, leave out empty sections and do not repeat yourself. It also explains the speaker labels (Tu, (Tú), Participantes) so the model only uses them when they add something. The placeholders {{SELF}}, {{SELF_NAMED}} and {{OTHERS}} are replaced with SpeakerLabels.ApplyToPrompt. The prompts are written in Spanish, and the labels the model must produce are always the Spanish ones. Step 6 translates them. 3. Repetition loops While generating, GenerateAsync compares each new line of 5 words or more with the previous 10 lines. Two lines are near-duplicates if their Jaccard index over words of 3 or more letters is ≥ 0.72. If 3 near-duplicates appear, it stops and runs the generation again with the strong sampling. 4. Parsing the answer (ParseResult) Removes Qwen3's … block if there is one (StripThinkBlock). Looks for the plain TITULO: / RESUMEN: format. It accepts accents, asterisks and any letter case. If not found, looks for the first JSON object with title and summary. Failing that, uses the first line as the title (60 characters at most) and the whole text as the summary. Then RemoveRepeatedLines removes near-duplicate lines within each section. 5. Missing sections If the summary has no Objetivos (goals) or Próximos pasos (next steps), it asks for them with the Goals and NextSteps prompts (at most 300 tokens each) over the same text. The model answers NINGUNO if there are none. At most 8 items are added, normalized as - …. 6. Labels in the interface language The model always writes the labels in Spanish: Proposito, Puntos clave, and so on. LocalizeSectionLabels replaces them with the SummaryLabel* keys of the requested language, except in Spanish, where they are left as they are. It also recognizes variants the model sometimes writes: with or without accents, singular ("Objetivo", "Próximo paso"), "Siguientes pasos" and "Tareas", which has its own label (SummaryLabelTasks) even though the prompt does not ask for it. How it is displayed ViewerViewModel runs the saved text through SummaryFormatter.Parse, which splits it into sections (SummarySection) for the viewer: It recognizes section labels in the five languages ("Puntos clave", "Key points", "Kernpunkte"…) and shows each title with the text of the current language and its icon. A summary generated in Spanish shows English titles if the interface is switched to English; the content does not change. - … lines are bullets, * … lines are topics, and bullets under a topic are indented one level. Progress ProgressTracker splits 100% between loading the model (150 units), each part (100 for prefill plus about 450 expected tokens) and the final prompt (100 plus about 900 tokens). The percentage stays at 99 until the end. Usage restrictions No summary is generated while recording or while a recording is being processed (CaptureStateChangedMessage). Recording cannot start while a summary is being generated (SummaryActivityChangedMessage). Closing the window during a summary asks for confirmation.

Messages They are all defined in ViewModels/Messages.cs and travel through WeakReferenceMessenger. Message Sender Receivers Meaning TargetSelectionChangedMessage(Target) Targets Shell, Recording The selected application changed. The shell navigates to its view and Recording takes it as the target. But they must not know the shell. IRecordingHost exposes exactly that: Member Used for IsRecording, IsBusy, StatusText, ElapsedText, IsTranscribingActive, TranscriptionProgressPercent State that is displayed. CanToggleRecording, RecordDisabledReason, CanStartRecordingFor(target) Whether recording is possible and, if not, why. SelectedTarget Selected application. StartRecordingForAsync(target) Selects the application with Targets.Select and only records if the selection really took effect in both Targets and Recording. RecordingHost implements it directly on top of RecordingViewModel and TargetsViewModel, and forwards their PropertyChanged. The floating window LiveTranslationViewModel only holds the window state. LiveTranslationFactory creates it for a specific application (Create(target, openMainWindow)), and it relies on three pieces: Piece Responsibility LiveSessionController Life cycle of the LiveTranscriptionSession: start it with the current models and settings, feed it audio, stop it, and marshal the session events to the UI thread. It drops events from a session that is no longer the current one. LiveTranscriptModel The lines shown (LiveLine), the transcription and translation drafts and their rules: what gets replaced, what is marked as not translated, when it is cleared. LiveMetricsPresenter The texts of the technical data strip. The live session starts when the window is open and its application is being recorded, no matter who started the recording. It stops when recording of that application stops. How the session works is in Live translation. The tray TrayMenuViewModel.Build(actions) builds the menu entries (TrayMenuEntry) according to the state: during the first run, only Open and Exit; when not recording, Start recording X for each watched application, enabled only if it can be recorded, and, if recording is blocked, the reason as a disabled entry; while recording, a status line with the live elapsed time and Stop recording X, which also shows the window; always, Live translation for X for each watched application, enabled only if it is open, or, if a floating window is open, only Close live translation for X. Record and stop actions run through a single AsyncRelayCommand. While one is running, the entries are disabled and extra clicks are ignored. TryRunExit prevents starting two exits at once. Threads ViewModels are updated on the UI thread. Events coming from other threads (process watcher, live session, worker process progress) go through IUiDispatcher or through a Progress created on the UI thread.

architecture/workers.html.title: Worker processes | LoopbackTranscriber
architecture/workers.html.summary:
Worker processes Whisper.net and LLamaSharp allocate native and GPU memory that is not always returned to the system when the model is released. To keep the main application from growing with each use, all inference runs in child processes: the same executable started in worker mode. Command line LoopbackTranscriber.exe --worker Argument Meaning --worker Marks the process as a worker. whisper, summary, whisper-live or translate-live. The JSON file with the job. Where the process writes the result. The application's PID, for the parent watchdog. WorkerProcess.CreateStartInfo builds it from Environment.ProcessPath. If the application runs as dotnet LoopbackTranscriber.dll, for example from the debugger, it adds the assembly path as the first argument. The process is created without a window and with standard output and standard error redirected. Program.Main recognizes the invocation with WorkerHost.IsWorkerInvocation: the second argument must be --worker and there must be at least 5. In that case it runs WorkerHost.Run and exits without creating App. Type Mode Job Result whisper batch WhisperJob WhisperJobResult summary batch SummaryJob SummaryJobResult whisper-live persistent LiveWhisperConfig over stdout translate-live persistent LiveTranslatorConfig over stdout Job files are written to %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber\worker\ with a GUID as the name: .job.json and .result.json, or .live.json for the persistent ones. They are deleted at the end. Parent watchdog When is passed, the worker starts a background thread that waits for that process to end. When it ends, or if it no longer exists, the worker exits with code 2. That way no worker outlives the application, even if it dies abruptly. WorkerProcess.RunAsync participant F as Worker folder

whisper or summary App->>F: Writes .job.json App->>W: Starts the process W->>F: Reads the job loop While working W-->>App: stdout "@@P 42.5" end alt Succeeds W->>F: Writes .result.json W-->>App: Exits with code 0 else Fails W->>F: Writes .result.json
with Error, ErrorKey and ErrorArgs W-->>App: Exits with code 1 else Exits without a result W-->>App: Exits with any code end Note over App: Waits up to 5 s
for the output to drain alt There is a result F->>App: Reads .result.json else There is no result Note over App: ErrorBackgroundProcessEnded
and the last 40 stderr lines in app.log end App->>F: Deletes both files Progress: @@P lines on standard output, in invariant culture with up to 3 decimals (WorkerProtocol.FormatProgress / TryParseProgress). Any other line is ignored. Result: the worker writes the JSON and exits with 0. Error: on failure, it writes to the result file an object with Error (the message) and, if the exception carried a localization key, ErrorKey and ErrorArgs, and exits with 1. The application turns that into an exception with the same key (UserError.FromWorker), so the user sees the message in their own language. No result: if the process ends without writing anything (because a driver hangs, or the C++ runtime is missing), ErrorBackgroundProcessEnded is thrown with the exit code. The last 40 lines of stderr are written to app.log (WorkerStderrTail). Cancellation: the CancellationToken kills the process tree. Once the process ends, the app waits at most 5 s for its output to drain. JSON contracts Type Fields WhisperJob WavPath, ModelPath, Language, FallbackLanguage, ThreadCount, StrictNoSpeech, UseGpu WhisperJobResult Language, Segments (each with StartTicks, EndTicks and Text), Error, ErrorKey, ErrorArgs SummaryJob TranscriptText, ModelPath, UiLanguage SummaryJobResult Title, Summary, Error, ErrorKey, ErrorArgs Persistent mode (whisper-live, translate-live) LiveWorkerClient starts the process with standard input redirected as UTF-8 without BOM, and talks to it line by line: Direction Format Application → worker (stdin) One JSON line per request: LiveWhisperRequest { Id, Audio } (base64 PCM) or LiveTranslateRequest { Id, Text, Context, Target }. Worker → application (stdout) @@L followed by a LiveWorkerMessage as JSON. LiveWorkerMessage: Field Meaning Ready true in the first message, once the model is loaded. Id The request it answers. 0 with Error means a start-up failure. Error Error for that request. The worker keeps running. Ms Inference milliseconds. Segments Transcribed segments (whisper-live). Text Translated text (translate-live). The client waits at most 180 s for Ready. Each request has its own TaskCompletionSource in a dictionary keyed by Id. Writes to stdin are serialized with a semaphore. Timeout per request: 60 s to transcribe and 30 s to translate. If the process ends, every pending request fails with ErrorBackgroundProcessEnded. LiveWorkerSupervisor decides whether to restart it. When the client is disposed, it closes stdin, kills the process tree and deletes the configuration file. Unhandled errors in the worker InstallUnhandledExceptionLogging writes the worker's unhandled exceptions and unobserved tasks to app.log, with its type in brackets (WorkerHost[whisper]: …). Every log line carries the PID, which tells you which process wrote it.

The language switch link replaces /es/ with /en/ in the current address, or the other way round, so it takes you to the same page in the other language. development/tests.html.title: Tests | LoopbackTranscriber
development/tests.html.summary: Tests LoopbackTranscriber.Tests uses xUnit 2.9.3 and targets net10.0-windows with WPF, because the ViewModels depend on WPF types such as DispatcherTimer. Tests run without a window, audio devices, models or worker processes: everything external is replaced by test doubles. Running Command Runs dotnet test LoopbackTranscriber.slnx -c Release All the tests. dotnet test LoopbackTranscriber.slnx --filter Category=Unit Only the unit tests. dotnet test LoopbackTranscriber.slnx --filter Category=Integration Only the integration tests. dotnet test LoopbackTranscriber.slnx --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RecordingWorkflow" The tests of one class, by name. In Visual Studio: Test → Test Explorer → Run All. To group by category, use Group By → Traits. Layout Folder or file Contents GlobalUsings.cs Common namespaces and the TranscriptSegment alias. Infrastructure\ Utilities shared by the tests. Fakes\ Test doubles for the application's interfaces. Models\ One file per type in Models\. Services\ One file per service. ViewModels\ One file per ViewModel. Each test class is named after the class it tests plus Tests. Each test follows the Situation_ExpectedResult shape, for example WhileRecording_No_ExitsAtOnce_KeepingTheAudioToProcessLater. Categories Each class has a [Trait(TestCategory.Name, …)] trait: Category Meaning Unit Pure logic: no disk, no clock, no threads. Runs in milliseconds. Integration Uses a temporary folder, real WAV files or real timing. Still fast and isolated. Infrastructure Type Used for TestEnvironment [ModuleInitializer] that runs before any test. Creates %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber.Tests\<pid>, redirects AppLog.LogPath there so nothing is written to the real log, and sets the language to Spanish. TempDirectory A temporary folder of each test's own. Deleted when disposed. TestSettings AppSettings with every folder inside the temporary one. CreateModelFiles creates fake 1-byte models so the application believes they are installed. WavFile Writes and reads test WAVs: tones, silence, PCM or float, deliberately broken headers, duration and format. Eventually.Until(condition, reason) Waits without blocking, checking the condition every 10 ms, for up to 5 s by default. If it is not met, fails with the reason. CollectingProgress<T> Synchronous IProgress<T> that stores the values. InterfaceLanguage.Use(lang) Changes the interface language and restores it when disposed. InterfaceLanguageTestGroup xUnit collection without parallelization. The language is global state, so tests that change it go in it. RecordingRig Assembles the whole recording flow with doubles: CaptureCoordinator, RecordingWorkflow, RecordingProcessor, RecordingViewModel, the failed recordings store and Teams as the application. Includes helpers such as StartRecordingAsync, WhisperSays and LeaveOrphan. ShellRig MainViewModel with all its children, on top of a RecordingRig. Test doubles Double Replaces What it allows FakeProcess IProcessCapture Writing a test WAV, delaying the start (StartGate), counting starts and setting the peak. FakeDevice IDeviceCapture Returning device tracks with any peak you like. FakeMic IMicCapture Simulating a microphone that starts or not (StartSucceeds). FakeWhisper IWhisperTranscriber Returning segments by file name and a detected language, holding the transcription (Gate) and recording the requests. FakeAudio IAudioPreparer Duration, activity and level maps, and noise gate failures. FakeSettingsStore ISettingsStore In-memory settings. Each read returns a copy, like the real service. Counts updates. FakeDialogs IDialogService Fixed answers to Yes/No and Yes/No/Cancel. Records errors and info messages. FakeTargetWatcher ITargetWatcher Marking applications as open or closed (SetRunning). FakeCustomApps ICustomAppsService Adding and removing applications. FakeSummarizer ISummarizer A fixed summary and a call counter. FakeLiveHost IRecordingHost A simulated recording for the floating window and the tray: delaying or failing the start, and reacting to the stop (OnStop). FakePageFactory IPageFactory Counting the pages created. FakeModelVerifier IModelVerifier Result or exception of the model verification. Guidelines No test touches the user's real state: not settings.json, %LocalAppData%, the log, nor real processes or devices. Services that save to disk take their path through the constructor, such as SettingsService(notices, settingsPath) or FailedRecordingStore(rootFolder). Tests pass them a path inside their TempDirectory. To wait for something asynchronous, use Eventually.Until, not Task.Delay with a fixed time. To control when an operation finishes, use a TaskCompletionSource (the doubles' Gates). Messages between ViewModels are tested with a WeakReferenceMessenger of each test's own, not WeakReferenceMessenger.Default. Expected texts are obtained with Strings.Instance.Get(...) or Format(...) instead of being written by hand, except when the translation itself is what is being tested. Do not use your real name in test data: the tests use pgomur.

guide/applications.html.title: Applications | LoopbackTranscriber
guide/applications.html.summary: Applications The Applications screen lets you choose which programs, besides Teams, appear in the sidebar so they can be recorded. Adding an application Open the application you want to record and make it play audio: join a call or play a video. In Applications, the Detected processes with audio section lists the processes that have an audio session right now. It refreshes on its own every 2 seconds while the screen is open, and also with Refresh. Applications that are already watched are not listed. Click Add. The application moves to Added for listening and appears in the sidebar. The name shown is the executable's description (for example, "Zoom Meetings") or, if it has none, the process name. That name is also the name of its transcripts folder. Added applications are saved in the settings with their process name (for example zoom or chrome) and are watched just like Teams. Tip For Google Meet or other meetings in the browser, add the browser (Chrome, Edge…). Keep in mind that all of the browser's audio is recorded, not just the meeting tab: close other tabs that play sound. Removing an application Click Remove under Added for listening. If the application has saved transcripts, it cannot be removed: delete them from the history first. Teams is built in and cannot be removed. How the process is chosen Many applications run several processes with the same name (Teams, browsers). The application: Finds the processes with that name and keeps the root of the tree, the one whose parent is not another of them. If one of those processes has an active audio session, prefers that one. Records that process and all its child processes, which is usually where call audio and browser tabs live.

guide/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | LoopbackTranscriber
guide/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Installation Run LoopbackTranscriberSetup-<version>.exe. The wizard is available in Spanish, English, Portuguese, German and Russian. If Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64) is missing, the installer downloads and installs it, unless it is already bundled in the installer itself. Whisper and the summary model need it. If it cannot be downloaded, setup continues and tells you where to install it manually. If the Visual C++ installer asks for a restart, the wizard offers it at the end. The application is installed in Program Files\LoopbackTranscriber. Your data is stored in %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber: see Data on disk. Note Only one instance can be open. If you open the application again while it is already running (for example, minimized to the tray), the window of the existing instance is shown. First start: downloading the models On startup, if either of the two models is missing (the first time, for example), the Before you start screen is shown: Model Used for Size Whisper large-v3-turbo (GGML, q5_1) Turning audio into text, and live transcription ~624 MB Qwen3-4B (GGUF, Q4_K_M) Summaries and live translation ~2.5 GB Click Download models. Both models download at the same time. Each download shows its progress and can be Paused, Resumed or Cancelled. A paused download continues where it left off; Cancel deletes what was downloaded. When it finishes, the SHA256 checksum of each file is checked. If it does not match, the file is discarded and you will have to download it again. Continue is only enabled once both are ready. Clicking it opens Settings so you can check your name and the languages. The models are stored in %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\models. You can change that folder in Settings. Tip On every start, the application checks in the background that the installed models are not damaged. If one is, it deletes it and shows this screen again so it can be downloaded again, unless a recording is in progress or being processed. Details in Models and integrity. Recommended settings before recording In Settings: Your name: shown in transcripts instead of "You". By default it is the first name of your Windows account. Meeting language: the language being spoken. If you do not choose one, the application language is used. If your meetings change language, choose Detect automatically. Application language: the language of the interface and of the summaries. Consent Only record and transcribe with the consent of the people taking part. You are responsible for informing them and for complying with the law in your country.

guide/live-translation.html.title: Live translation | LoopbackTranscriber
guide/live-translation.html.summary: Live translation Live translation opens a floating window that shows, while recording, what the participants are saying and its translation. It helps you follow a meeting in a language you do not master. Opening it From the application view, with the Live translation button. It is only enabled while the application is open. If the floating window is already open for that application, the same button closes it. From the tray icon (with the main window minimized or hidden): right-click → Live translation for X. While the window is open, the same entry becomes Close live translation for X. Only one floating window can be open at a time: opening it for another application closes the previous one. It appears against the right edge of the screen, vertically centered. Using it In Translate to:, choose the target language: Spanish, English, Portuguese, German or Russian. The choice is remembered. Click Start recording and translating. A normal recording of that application starts and the window begins showing text within a few seconds. Click Stop recording to stop. The recording is processed like any other, the window shows the progress, and the full transcript is saved to the history. If the recording of that application is started some other way (the main window or the tray) while the floating window is open, live translation starts anyway. While someone is speaking, a draft appears and keeps being corrected. When there is a pause, the sentence is fixed as a final line and translated. Long sentences are split over several lines. The status line shows "Recording · 00:00" and, while the models load, "Loading the speech model…" and "loading the translator…". When not recording, it shows "Idle". Window controls Control What it does Opacity Makes the window more or less transparent, between 30% and 100%. Remembered. Always on top Keeps the window above all others. On when the window opens. Open Loopback Transcriber Shows the main window. Close Closes the floating window. Any recording in progress keeps going. Technical data When Show technical data is on, a strip at the bottom shows: Signal: the level of the application audio, or "no audio from the app". Last chunk (or draft): seconds of audio, seconds of processing, and the delay since that speech ended. Translation: translation time and delay. Settings In the sidebar, Live translation opens the floating window settings, with a preview: Setting Default Translate to The last one chosen; the first time, the application language Show the original text below the translation Yes Text size 19 (from 14 to 32) Window opacity 100% (from 30% to 100%) Show technical data (signal and timings) Yes Changes apply immediately to the floating window, if it is open. Limitations Only the application audio is transcribed live, not your microphone. Your voice does appear in the final transcript. Translation uses the same model as summaries (Qwen3-4B). If it is not downloaded, the window only shows the transcription and says "no translation: the summary model is missing". If the speech model is missing, the window says "The speech model is missing. Download it in Settings.". If the computer cannot keep up, the oldest chunks are dropped first so the delay does not build up. A sentence may be missing from the window, but never from the final transcript, which is made afterwards from the full audio. How it works internally is described in Architecture: live translation.

guide/recording.html.title: Recording a meeting | LoopbackTranscriber
guide/recording.html.summary: Recording a meeting Choosing the application The sidebar shows the applications being watched. Teams is included by default. You can add any other application that plays audio (Zoom, the browser for Meet, Discord…) from Applications. The list is refreshed every 1.5 seconds. An application can only be recorded while it is open. If it is, the status says "X detected. Press "Start recording" to start.". If not, "X doesn't seem to be open yet. Open it and select it again.". Starting and stopping Select the application and click Start recording. The status changes to "Listening to X..." and the timer starts. Click Stop recording when you are done. The recording is processed straight away: "Processing audio..." "Checking the transcription model..." "Transcribing... N%" "Transcript ready and saved" The transcript appears in the viewer and is saved to the history. You can also start and stop from the tray icon: right-click → Start recording X / Stop recording X. The icon only appears while the window is minimized or closed with the X. Stopping from the tray shows the window, so you can follow the processing. While recording, hovering over the icon shows "Loopback Transcriber - Recording X". Note If you close the recorded application while recording, the recording stops and is processed as if you had clicked Stop recording. What is recorded Three sources are recorded at the same time: Track What it contains What it is for Application Only the audio played by the chosen process and its child processes The voices of the other participants. It is the main source. Audio output Everything played through the Windows default outputs: the general one and, if it is a different one, the communications one. Each on its own track. Fallback if the application track turns out silent. Microphone The default microphone Your voice, on a separate track. When recording stops, if the application track has no signal, the loudest output track is used instead. The microphone is transcribed separately and aligned in time with the other track. That is how the transcript tells Participants apart from You, or your name followed by "(You)". If the microphone cannot be opened, recording continues without it and you are warned: "Your microphone is not being recorded: the transcript will only include the participants.". If it opens but only captures silence, its track is dropped when recording stops and the transcript has no speaker labels. While a summary is being generated You cannot start recording while an AI summary is being generated, because both compete for the GPU and memory. The button says so: "You can't record while an AI summary is being generated." If no text is detected If Whisper returns no text: Recording shorter than 20 seconds: it is assumed nothing was said. The viewer shows "(No text was detected in the audio)", the status changes to "Transcript ready." and nothing is saved: neither text nor audio. Recording of 20 seconds or more: it is treated as a failure (see below) and the audio is kept. If something goes wrong Except in the case above, the application never deletes the audio of a recording that could not be transcribed. If processing fails, the status shows the error and the folder where the audio was saved, and the application's view shows the Unprocessed recording banner with two icon buttons, which show their name on hover: Retry: processes it again with the current settings. Not available while recording, while another recording is being processed or while a summary is being generated. Discard: deletes the audio for good, after asking for confirmation. Each unprocessed recording shows up in its application's view. Those recovered without knowing which application they belonged to show up as "Meeting" in every application's view. The same happens if the application closes during a recording, the computer shuts down or an unexpected error occurs. When you open it again, the recording shows up as unprocessed. The specific cases are in Reliability. Closing the application The window's X does not close the application: it hides it to the tray, so you can keep recording. The first time, a notification explains this. Clicking the icon shows the window again. To really exit: right-click the tray icon → Exit. If you exit while recording, you are asked what to do: Yes: stop the recording, process it with the window visible, and exit when done. No: exit now and keep the audio unprocessed for next time. Cancel: keep recording. If a recording is being processed, you are asked whether to wait for it to finish and then exit. If you say no, the application stays open.

guide/settings.html.title: Settings | LoopbackTranscriber
guide/settings.html.summary: Settings The settings screen General Setting What it does Default Your name Labels what you say as "Name (You)" instead of "You". Up to 20 characters. Saved 0.7 s after you stop typing. If you leave it empty, "You" is used. The first name of your Windows account or, if it has none, your user name with a capital initial. Application language Language of the interface and of the summaries: Spanish, English, Portuguese, German or Russian. Applies immediately. The Windows language if it is one of those five, otherwise English. Meeting language The language being spoken, for your microphone and the participants: Detect automatically or one of the five languages. Follows the application language until you choose another one. Translucent interface Applies the Windows 11 Mica effect to the window background. Not applied on the first-run screen. Off Tip Setting a fixed meeting language gives better results than automatic detection if you always speak the same language. Use Detect automatically if it changes from one meeting to the next. How detection works is explained in Processing a recording. AI models Two sections, Transcription and AI summary, show each model, its size on disk or that it is missing, and a button to download it: Download transcription model and Download summary model. If a model is already in the folder, its integrity is checked instead of downloading it again. The status refreshes on its own when files appear in or disappear from the models folder. Downloads cannot be paused here. If one is interrupted, for example by closing the application, the next download continues where it left off. Folders and saving Folder Default Models folder %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\models Transcripts folder %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\transcripts Open shows it in Explorer and Change picks another one. Important Changing a folder does not move its contents. If you change the models folder, move the files yourself or download them again. If you change the transcripts folder, the history will only show what is in the new one. On uninstall, folders you changed are not deleted. About A link to the author's GitHub profile, the legal notice (consent to record, local processing, and that summaries can contain errors) and Third-party software licenses, which opens THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. The settings file All settings are stored in %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\settings.json. The application writes it by itself and you do not need to edit it. It is described here for troubleshooting, and because three advanced settings only exist in this file. Key Type Meaning ModelSize string Whisper model. Defaults to turbo, the only one with a pinned SHA256 checksum. Any other value (tiny, base, small, medium, large) only works if ggml-<value>.bin is already in models\whisper, and it is not verified. If it is not there, an error is raised. The first run and the startup verification always use turbo, and any change saved from Settings resets this value to turbo. ModelsFolder string Models folder. TranscriptsFolder string Transcripts folder. MeetingLanguage string "" follows the application language, auto detects the language, and es, en, pt, de or ru fix one. UiLanguage string es, en, pt, de or ru. TranslucentUi boolean Translucent interface. UserName string Your name in transcripts. In the labels, colons are replaced with spaces. UserNameInitialized boolean The Windows name has already been suggested. It is not suggested again even if you clear the name. TrayHintShown boolean The "still running in the tray" notification has already been shown. FirstRunSetupCompleted boolean The initial model download has been completed. CustomApps list Added applications: Id (custom:<lowercase process>), DisplayName and ProcessName. LiveTranslationLanguage string Target language of live translation. LiveWindowOpacity number Opacity of the floating window, from 0.3 to 1. LiveShowOriginal boolean Show the original below the translation. LiveShowMetrics boolean Show the technical data strip. LiveTextSize number Text size of the floating window, from 14 to 32. LiveAudioContext integer Advanced. Whisper audio context size for live transcription. 0 uses the model's own. Smaller values reduce latency at the cost of accuracy. LiveFlashAttention boolean Advanced. Turns on flash attention for live Whisper. If the model does not load with it, it is retried without it. If you edit the file by hand, do it with the application closed. The application only reads the file at startup and, on every settings change, rewrites all of it from what it holds in memory, so your changes would be lost. What happens if the file is damaged If settings.json is not valid JSON, it is moved aside as settings.json.corrupt-<date>, the defaults are used and you are told: "The settings could not be read and have been reset to their defaults." If it cannot be written (full disk, no permissions, antivirus), it is attempted three times. The changes are kept in memory, retried on the next change and on exit, and you are told once. Writing is atomic: a settings.json.tmp is written and then replaces the original. A power cut never leaves a half-written file.
