guide/transcripts.html.summary: Transcripts and summaries Where they are Transcripts (sidebar): every saved transcript, from any application. History, in each application's view: only that application's transcripts. Each item shows the title (the summary's title if there is one, otherwise the application name), the date and audio duration (dd/MM HH:mm · m:ss, or h:mm:ss from one hour on) and a 100-character excerpt. The excerpt comes from the summary if it exists and otherwise from the beginning of the transcript. If there is neither, it shows "(Empty transcript)". The list refreshes on its own when the transcripts folder changes, including when you copy or delete files by hand. Open folder opens the transcripts folder in Explorer. Note An application's History shows the recordings whose folder carries exactly its name. If the application name contains characters that are not allowed in a file name (\ / : * ? " < > |), its recordings are saved with those characters replaced by _ and only show up in Transcripts. Searching Both lists have a Search transcripts and summaries box. It searches the title, the application name, the date (dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm and yyyy-MM-dd), the summary and the full text of the transcript. Case- and accent-insensitive: resume finds "Résumé". Several words: all of them must appear, anywhere. In quotes, an exact phrase: "next week". The search starts 300 ms after you stop typing. If nothing matches, the list says "No results". Filtering The Filter button opens a panel to narrow the list: From / To: dates included. Minimum duration (minutes): leaves out shorter recordings. Recordings without saved audio are left out too while this filter is set. Filters apply immediately. Apply closes the panel and Clear filters removes them all. While a filter is active, the Filter button is highlighted. Each list (Transcripts and each application's History) has its own filters and its own search. The viewer When you open a transcript, the viewer has two tabs: Transcript: the text as a conversation. Each paragraph shows who is speaking (Participants, You or your name (You)). As in a chat, your turns are on the right and the participants' on the left. AI summary: the summary, if there is one. Clear viewer closes it. If the recording only has audio, the viewer says so instead of showing text. Generating a summary In the AI summary tab, click Summarize. Progress is shown as a percentage. The summary is written in the application language, even if the meeting was in another one, and contains: Title: eight words at most. Purpose: what the conversation is about and why it took place. Key points: between 5 and 12, with concrete details. Topics: only if several subjects were discussed, or one in a lot of detail. Goals: what someone wants to achieve or commits to doing. Next steps: meetings, dates and follow-ups that were agreed. Sections with no content are left out. Once generated, the summary's title replaces the application name in the list. Regenerate replaces the summary with a new one. Section titles are always shown in the current application language, each with its icon. The content stays in the language it was generated in. Note Summaries cannot be generated while recording or while a recording is being processed. If you close the application while one is being generated, you are asked to confirm, because that summary would be lost. If the summary model is missing, the viewer says "The summary model is missing. Download it in Settings to generate summaries.". A recording that only has audio cannot be summarized. AI summaries can contain errors: review them before using them. Transcribing again Transcribe again processes the saved audio again with the current settings (language, your name) and replaces the text. It asks for confirmation first. Use it, for example, after changing the meeting language. It is only in the viewer of each application's History, not in Transcripts. It is only available if the recording has its audio (.wav), and not while recording or while another recording is being processed. The summary is not changed. You can regenerate it afterwards. The file's header line is kept. Deleting Tick the boxes of the transcripts you want to delete and click Delete. You are asked to confirm. The whole folder of each recording is deleted: text, audio and summary. If it was the last one for that application, the application folder is deleted as well. This cannot be undone. A transcript cannot be deleted while its summary is being generated. Files of each recording Each saved recording is a folder inside the transcripts folder: transcripts\ Teams\ Teams_20261018_093000\ Teams_20261018_093000.md text (Markdown) Teams_20261018_093000.wav meeting audio Teams_20261018_093000_mic.wav your microphone, if it was recorded Teams_20261018_093000.recording.json microphone offset Teams_20261018_093000.summary.json summary, if one was generated The format of each file is described in Data on disk.

guide/troubleshooting.html.summary: Troubleshooting Where to look File Contents %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\logs\app.log Log of the application and its worker processes. Each line has the date, level (INFO, WARN, ERROR) and PID. Once it passes 1 MB it is renamed to app.log.1 and a new one starts. %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\live-metrics.log Live translation timings, chunk by chunk, and a SUMMARY line at the end of each session. It is emptied once it passes 512 KB. When the application closes because of an unexpected error, the message shows the path of the log. Whisper and the summary model run in worker processes: the same LoopbackTranscriber.exe started with --worker <type>. To tell them apart in Task Manager, open the Details tab and add the Command line column. The types are whisper, summary, whisper-live and translate-live. Common problems "No text was detected in N s of audio (possible model or GPU failure)" The recording is 20 seconds or longer and Whisper returned no text. The audio is kept as an unprocessed recording. Click Retry. If it happens again, update your GPU driver. Whisper uses Vulkan when available. Check in the log which track was used. Look for falling back to device track and ProcessLoopbackRecorder: packets=…, peak=…. A peak of 0 means the application played no audio. For recordings shorter than 20 seconds, an empty transcript is not treated as an error: nothing is saved and the audio is discarded. The application track is silent Some applications play call audio from a process that is not a child of the main one. In that case the application uses the audio output track, which includes any other sound on the computer. To avoid it, add in Applications the process that shows up under Detected processes with audio during the call. "The background process ended unexpectedly (code N)" The Whisper or summary process ended without returning a result. The log includes the last 40 lines of its error output. The most common cause is a missing Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable (x64). Install it from https://aka.ms/vs/17/release/vc_redist.x64.exe. Code 2 means the process ended because the main application closed. "The downloaded model (…) does not match the expected checksum and was discarded" The download arrived damaged or incomplete. Download it again from Settings. If it keeps happening, check whether a proxy or an antivirus is modifying downloads. "The model … could not be loaded" The file exists but cannot be loaded. On the next use its SHA256 is checked again: if it is damaged it is deleted and can be downloaded again. "Your microphone is not being recorded" The default microphone could not be opened. In Windows Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, check that desktop apps have access, and that there is a default microphone. "The recovery file could not be created…" The temporary folder (%TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber) could not be written to. Recording continues, but if the application closes abruptly the recording cannot be recovered. Check free space and permissions. "An interrupted recording could not be recovered…" At startup, audio from an interrupted recording was found but could not be moved to unprocessed recordings. The audio is still in %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber and is retried on every start. "The recording could not be started: …" Capturing the application's audio could not start. The status shows the reason after the colon. Check that the application is still open, select it again and retry. The details are in app.log, on the line RecordingViewModel.StartRecordingAsync: failed to start recording. "The background process could not be started." The application could not launch a worker process or did not get its answer. Exit the application from the tray and open it again. If it happens again, check app.log. "The … model could not be checked" or "The installed models could not be checked…" At startup a model could not be read to check its fingerprint, for example because another program has it open or permissions are missing. The model is not deleted and is checked again before it is used. "The summary could not be generated: …" or "The recording could not be transcribed again: …" The reason appears after the colon and is usually one of the errors on this page, such as a worker process or model failure. "The audio of this recording was not found." means the recording's .wav has been deleted or moved. "The transcript could not be read…", "The transcript … could not be deleted…" or "The recording could not be deleted…" The file or folder is open in another program or you do not have permissions on it. Close it and try again. If the search fails for the same reason, the list shows "The search could not be completed". A transcript does not show up in the history If a recording folder cannot be read, you are told "A transcript could not be read and is not shown in the history", with its path. A folder only appears in the history if it contains a .md, .txt or .wav with the same name as the folder. Starting from scratch Exit the application from the tray. Delete %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber\settings.json. To start completely from scratch, delete the whole %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber folder: transcripts and models will be lost. When uninstalling, the uninstaller offers to delete that folder and %TEMP%\LoopbackTranscriber.

index.html.summary: LoopbackTranscriber Windows desktop application · Open source (MIT) Record, transcribe and summarize your meetings without anything leaving your computer. It records the audio of one specific application (Teams, Zoom, Meet in the browser…) together with your microphone. It then transcribes it with Whisper, tells what you say apart from what the others say, and, when you ask for it, writes a summary with a language model. While you record, it can also show the meeting translated in a floating window. Getting started How it works inside GitHub System 64-bit Windows 11 10.0.22000 or later Acceleration Vulkan GPU Without one, CPU (slower) Transcription Whisper large-v3-turbo ~624 MB model Summary and translation Qwen3-4B ~2.5 GB model Internet Only to download models Everything else is local Built with WPF · .NET 10 MVVM pattern Languages ES EN PT DE RU Interface, meetings (or automatic detection) and translation How to use it Optional: open live translation to follow the meeting translated while you record. Pick the application Teams is built in. Zoom, the browser or others are added in Applications. See the guide Record Press Start recording (or use the tray icon). The application, the default audio output and your microphone are recorded at the same time. See the guide Get the transcript When you press Stop recording, Whisper transcribes it and, if your microphone was recorded, separates Participants from You. It is saved in the history. See the guide Summarize In the AI summary tab, press Summarize: title, key points, goals and next steps. See the guide Features Each feature links to its user guide and its technical explanation. Per-application recording Only the audio of the chosen program, plus your microphone on a separate track. If that track turns out silent, it uses the default audio output. Guide · Technical Any application Teams is built in. Add Zoom, Discord or the browser (for Meet) from the processes that are playing audio. Guide · Technical Transcription with Whisper Whisper large-v3-turbo, on a Vulkan GPU when there is one. Fixed language or automatic detection. Filters hallucinations, repetitions and echo. Guide · Technical Who is speaking Your microphone is transcribed separately and aligned with the meeting. Each paragraph says Participants or You, with your name in front if you set one. Guide · Technical History and search Search the title, application, date, summary and full text, ignoring case and accents. Filter by date and duration, and transcribe again with the current settings. Guide · Technical AI summary Qwen3-4B writes a title, purpose, key points, topics, goals and next steps, in the application language. Guide · Technical Live translation Floating window with what the participants say and its translation into Spanish, English, Portuguese, German or Russian. Guide · Technical Nothing is lost If something goes wrong (an error, an exit, a shutdown or a crash), the audio is kept as an unprocessed recording so it can be retried. Guide · Technical Privacy and data What uses the internet and where your files end up. Everything stays on your computer Audio, transcripts and summaries never leave it. The application only goes online to download the two models, from a fixed Hugging Face revision and checking their SHA256. The installer may also download Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable if it is missing. Only record with the consent of the people taking part. Models and integrity Where everything is stored In %LocalAppData%\LoopbackTranscriber: settings, models, transcripts, unprocessed recordings and log. The models and transcripts folders can be changed in Settings. Each recording is a folder with the text in Markdown (.md) and the audio (.wav), plus, when there are any, your microphone (_mic.wav) and the summary (.summary.json).
